description:
PARDIG (Precipitation AI Reanalysis - Densely Inferred GPM) is an
experimental dataset of global AI-driven precipitation estimates by Google
DeepMind and Google Research, produced by the model described in: [Global
Precipitation Estimates Learned from Sparse Satellite Observations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13941).

PARDIG is produced by an AI model that is trained to predict precipitation
estimates from the Combined Radar-Radiometer Algorithm (CORRA), part of the
NASA/JAXA Global Precipitation Measurement (GPM) Core Observatory.
PARDIG-LR relies on ECMWF's ERA5, NOAA's GridSat-B1, and a global mosaic of
polar-orbiting (LEO) microwave sounder observations as its inputs. PARDIG
precipitation estimates are provided at a 15 minute cadence and 0.1°
spatial resolution.

This image collection provides the full historical archive of PARDIG-LR
(Long-Record) from 1999 through 2023. The dataset is also available in Zarr
format in our Google Cloud Storage bucket (`gs://pardig_1/LR/`). The
companion dataset, PARDIG-NRT (Near-Real-Time), is also available on
[Earth Engine](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/projects_gcp-public-data-weathernext_assets_PARDIG_1_NRT)
and on Google Cloud Storage (`gs://pardig_1/NRT/`).

Both datasets are publicly available in the Earth Engine Data Catalog and
on Google Cloud Storage. Users can access them via their Google Cloud
account immediately, without needing to explicitly apply for access.

For more details about PARDIG and related products, visit the
[Developer Guide](https://developers.google.com/weathernext/guides/pardig).

**Acknowledgements**

This experimental dataset was generated by a model using data and products
of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), as well
as additional third-party providers. For a full list of attribution and
acknowledgements, please see our [acknowledgements page](https://storage.googleapis.com/weathernext-public/pardig-attributions-acknowledgements.pdf).
